title: Encryption Governance: Operator SOP and SIEM Export Mapping
content:
Purpose:
This operator-facing playbook consolidates runbook steps, RBAC v2 role mappings, the canonical audit log schema we emit for key operations, and SIEM export mapping for ingestion in Splunk/Elastic/Datadog. It is intended for on-call operators, security reviewers, and automation engineers who implement evidence automation for compliance audits (SOC2/ISO/PCI).

Scope and intent:
- Covers tenant & platform key lifecycle for hosted and dedicated deployments (BYOK onboarding, HSM-backed root keys, envelope key rotations, data-key refresh).
- Describes RBAC v2 roles, least privilege operations, and suggested policy expressions.
- Provides the canonical audit schema (fields + examples) and mappings to common SIEM fields.
- Contains an operator SOP for scheduled and emergency rotations and a checklist for evidence exports.

High-level key hierarchy (operator summary):
- Platform Root (HSM) — hardware-protected root used only for wrapping/unwrapping tenant root keys and signing evidence manifests.
- Tenant Root / Customer Master Key (CMK) — customer-assigned or Redwood-managed; used to wrap intermediate keys.
- Service/envelope keys — short-lived keys used by runtime for token hashing, caching, and transport encryption.
- Data keys — per-blob/per-file keys managed by the keystore and rotated frequently.

RBAC v2 roles and minimum allowed actions (operator cheat-sheet):
- role:crypto-operator (team:security-ops)
  - purpose: run rotations, view audit evidence, trigger rewraps
  - allowed_actions: ["kms:RotateKey","kms:ScheduleRotation","kms:CreateRewrapJob","evidence:Export","logs:ViewAudit"]
  - denied_actions: ["kms:ExportRawKey","kms:BypassHSM"]
- role:key-admin (team:platform-crypto)
  - purpose: full lifecycle management for platform-generated keys
  - allowed_actions: ["kms:CreateKey","kms:DeleteKey","kms:UpdateKeyPolicy","kms:GrantAccess"]
  - constraints: require 2-step approval for tenant-visible key deletion
- role:key-approver (team:legal, compliance)
  - purpose: approve BYOK onboarding / key escrow requests
  - allowed_actions: ["requests:ApproveBYOK","evidence:SignAcceptance"]
- role:svc-kms-broker (machine identity)
  - purpose: perform wrap/unwrap during runtime path
  - allowed_actions: ["kms:WrapKey","kms:UnwrapKey","kms:GenerateDataKey"]
  - token_constraints: short TTL, pinned to instance or connection fingerprint
- role:auditor (team:security-audit)
  - purpose: read-only audit access for compliance
  - allowed_actions: ["logs:QueryAudit","evidence:DownloadArtifacts"]

Policy notes for operators:
- All sensitive actions (RotateKey, ExportWrappedKey, GrantAccess) must include an authorization context: correlation_id, ticket_id, approver_id.
- Enforce attribute-based conditions where possible: source_ip_range, agent_fingerprint, mfa_verified.
- Any action that results in key material export must create an evidence manifest signed by the HSM key.

BYOK onboarding flow (operator steps):
1) Customer request received (ticket created) — assign ticket and attach BYOK metadata template.
2) Validate public key blob: ensure key format (PKCS#8/PEM), verify size & algorithm.
3) Policy sanity checks: allowed algorithms, expiration, and rotation policy.
4) Create temporary onboarding job: create tenant placeholder key in keystore with state=PROVISIONING.
5) Customer/partner performs key prove-of-possession challenge (signed nonce).
6) Operator approves in UI (requires key-approver approval) -> state=ACTIVE.
7) Emit evidence: onboarding-manifest.json signed by HSM. Store manifest and signed certificate in evidence-bucket and index into SIEM.

HSM fallback and dual-control pattern:
- Primary: HSM cluster in region (FIPS-validated).
- Fallback: remote HSM cluster in separate availability zone with automated quorum check.
- Dual-control for unwrapping platform roots: require two operator roles or operator + service principal.
- Emergency unseal: documented, time-limited breakout windows logged with high-fidelity evidence and privileged approval.

Rotation policy (recommended defaults):
- Data keys: rotate every 7–30 days (depending on data sensitivity).
- Envelope keys: rotate every 90 days or after N rewraps (N configurable).
- Tenant root (BYOK): customer-configurable; default policy recommends 1 year with automated non-disruptive rewrap.
- HSM root: rotate per vendor guidance (firmware/slot rotation) and on firmware upgrade, with full test vector validation.

Operator SOP: scheduled rotation (non-disruptive):
- Step 0: Prechecks
  - Verify system health: serving runtime > 99.9% last 6h, request queue < threshold.
  - Ensure evidence-bucket has >48h redundancy and SIEM pipeline healthy.
- Step 1: Create rotation job
  - Create job with correlation_id and ticket reference, set rollout window and canary subset.
- Step 2: Canary rewrap
  - Rewrap 1% of traffic (canary tenants) and run smoke tests against canary. Validate integrity of KV caches.
- Step 3: Gradual rollout
  - Expand to 10%, 50%, 100% with 30–60 minute observation windows. Abort on errors or high error_rate delta.
- Step 4: Validation
  - Verify metrics: unwrap latency, cache hit ratio, request error rate, and audit log entries for all rewrap operations.
- Step 5: Evidence export
  - Generate rotation-manifest.json (signed by HSM), store artifacts and index to SIEM with ticket and correlation_id.

Operator SOP: emergency rotation (compromise suspected):
- Immediate actions: freeze new key grants, move impacted keys to state=QUARANTINED, notify security & account teams.
- Create emergency rotation job with high priority and dual approval.
- Run full-backfill to re-encrypt affected ciphertext using new keys.
- Evidence: collect raw audit streams, HSM log snapshots, rewrap job deltas and sign them.

Audit log schema (canonical) — required fields (emit for every key operation):
- timestamp: ISO8601 string (e.g. 2026-01-18T15:43:21Z)
- event_id: UUID
- correlation_id: string (operator ticket or automation id)
- request_id: string (API gateway request id)
- principal_id: string (user:alice or svc:svc-kms-broker)
- principal_type: enum [user, service, system]
- actor_role: RBAC role name performing action
- action: enum [CreateKey, RotateKey, Rewrap, Wrap, Unwrap, GenerateDataKey, DeleteKey, GrantAccess, RevokeAccess, ExportEvidence]
- resource_type: enum [HSMSlot, TenantKey, EnvelopeKey, DataKey]
- resource_id: opaque id
- key_version: semantic version or epoch (e.g. v2026-01-09-3)
- key_state: enum [PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, ROTATING, QUARANTINED, DECOMMISSIONED]
- outcome: enum [success, failure]
- outcome_code: short string (e.g. KMS-ERR-1023)
- duration_ms: integer
- hsm_slot: optional string
- hsm_firmware: optional string
- evidence_artifact_id: id pointing to signed artifact in evidence-bucket
- request_payload_hash: sha256 hex
- response_signature: base64 (when operation signed by HSM)
- request_source_ip: ip
- request_user_agent: string
- approver_ids: list of principal ids (if approval required)
- notes: free text

Example audit log event (as emitted):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-18T15:43:21Z",
  "event_id": "7d6b3e7a-fb3d-4b9a-9c12-5aee1f2c6a2b",
  "correlation_id": "ROT-20260118-9987",
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "principal_id": "alice@redwood.com",
  "principal_type": "user",
  "actor_role": "crypto-operator",
  "action": "RotateKey",
  "resource_type": "TenantKey",
  "resource_id": "tenant_1234:cmk_7a9b",
  "key_version": "v2026-01-09-3",
  "key_state": "ROTATING",
  "outcome": "success",
  "duration_ms": 1243,
  "hsm_slot": "hsm-cluster-1/slot-02",
  "evidence_artifact_id": "ev-20260118-rot-9987",
  "request_payload_hash": "a3f5c1d7...",
  "response_signature": "MEUCIQDJ...",
  "approver_ids": ["ravi.shah@redwood.com"],
  "notes": "Canary rotation; all checks green"
}

SIEM export mapping (recommended):
- Canonical -> Splunk (KV ingest)
  - _time = timestamp
  - event_id = event_id
  - host = hsm_slot OR resource_id host portion
  - user = principal_id
  - action = action
  - resource = resource_id
  - result = outcome
  - evidence_id = evidence_artifact_id
  - duration_ms = duration_ms
- Canonical -> Elastic Common Schema (ECS)
  - @timestamp = timestamp
  - event.id = event_id
  - event.action = action
  - event.outcome = outcome
  - user.name = principal_id
  - service.name = "redwood-kms"
  - service.type = "kms"
  - cloud.instance.id = hsm_slot (if HSM-hosted)
- Canonical -> Datadog
  - timestamp -> dd.timestamp
  - host -> tags:host
  - event.action -> title
  - evidence_artifact_id -> body or extra_tags

Operator checklist for evidence automation (to produce audit package for auditors):
- Collect: rotation-manifest.json (signed), job logs (rotation job id), full audit stream slice (event_id list), HSM debug snapshot (if available), rewrap deltas.
- Hash & sign: compute sha256 of artifacts and sign with HSM signing key (response_signature).
- Store: upload artifacts to evidence-bucket under path: /evidence/<tenant>/<ticket>/<correlation_id>/ and set retention tags.
- Index: emit index event to SIEM with evidence_artifact_id, ticket_id, approvers list, and signed manifest.
- Export: produce zipped export for auditors with README.md (includes verification commands and sample verification keys).

Retention and encryption-at-rest design notes (operator guidance):
- Evidence artifacts: retain 7 years for enterprise customers who require extended retention; default 1 year for standard. Mark artifacts with retention-policies and immutable flags on object storage.
- At rest: all artifacts and keys are stored encrypted with tenant-root-wrapping keys. Evidence manifests are additionally signed by HSM signing key.
- Database encryption: use envelope encryption for PII columns in the metadata DB. Keys rotated on the same cadence as service envelope keys.

Incident runbook (suspected key compromise):
1) Triage: gather audit slice for last 72h, freeze key grants, escalate to incident-commander.
2) Contain: put impacted keys in QUARANTINED state and disable unwrap endpoints for them.
3) Rotate: generate new keys, re-encrypt affected ciphertext, and deploy new wrapping.
4) Evidence: snapshot HSM logs, collect all export artifacts, lock down evidence-bucket (read-only) and sign manifest.
5) Postmortem: run cryptographic proof checks, produce a signed report, and schedule customer communications per contract.

Operator troubleshooting quick tips:
- Missing audit entries: check log forwarder health, verify local buffer retention in keystore (usually 1h) and inspect backlog consumer.
- Rewrap failures: common causes: stale KV cache, incompatible key policy (policy version mismatch), HSM overload (observe hsm_queue).
- Performance regressions after rotation: verify chosen kernel/quantization profile for model-serving if relying on runtime caches — rotation should not change runtime kernels but may affect cache hit ratios.

Appendix — sample SIEM queries:
- Splunk: find failed rotates in last 24h
  index=kms_audit action=RotateKey outcome=failure | stats count by resource_id, outcome_code
- Elastic (KQL): high-latency rotations
  event.action: "RotateKey" and duration_ms:>10000 | sort by duration_ms desc
- Datadog (Log query): evidence exports last 7 days by tenant tag
  logs("service:kms AND evidence_artifact_id:*", from:now-7d).group_by(["@tenant_id"])

Appendix — verification commands for auditors (examples):
- Verify signed manifest (local):
  openssl dgst -sha256 -verify hsm_pubkey.pem -signature manifest.sig rotation-manifest.json
- Verify evidence object hash:
  sha256sum rotation-manifest.json | grep <stored-hash>

Notes and outstanding items for automation backlog:
- Automate ticket -> correlation_id enrichment for all rotation jobs (SECOPS-712).
- Add HSM firmware version to every audit event (pending HSM SDK patch).
- Support CEF mapping for legacy SIEMs (low priority).

Contact and escalation list:
- Primary crypto ops: crypto-oncall@redwood.com
- HSM vendor POC: hsm-support@vendor.example
- Compliance lead: lucia.fernandez@redwood.com

End of operator cheat-sheet.
